fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of approach.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving from either direction can identify the correct access point without delay.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain clear sightlines from the road to the main residence.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles closest to the main residence to allow responder equipment and personnel to reach the front of the structure.
• Cut back dense vegetation that limits visibility between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can visually confirm both buildings from a central point on the property.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence and the detached structure, including any gates or walkways connecting them.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of vegetation, equipment, or other obstacles.
• Mark or number the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence when communicating during an incident.
• If any gates exist along the walkway or between structures, keep them unlocked or secured with a break-away latch to allow rapid responder movement across the property.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure to give responders room to work around all sides of the building.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles from around the base of the structure and any nearby outbuildings.
• Trim lower branches from large trees surrounding the structure to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Cut back shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from each other and from larger trees to reduce connected patches of vegetation.
• Clear dead branches, fallen limbs, and leaf litter from the ground around the structure.
• Remove or relocate any wood, lumber, or organic material stored next to exterior walls.
• Trim overhanging tree branches that extend directly above the roofline.
• Keep the single access route free of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Clear woody debris from the edges of the driveway to keep the travel surface fully passable.
• Maintain open ground between the base of large trees and the exterior walls of the structure.
• Remove dead shrubs or dried plant material within the immediate area around the structure.
